policy_title: Commence Royal Commission of Inquiry into Social Care
stated: Reform UK will commence a Royal Commission of Inquiry into the social care system to develop a national plan for a sustainable sector, focusing on flexibility, tax incentives, VAT breaks, reduced waste, and a single funding stream. More funding will be provided once a national plan is agreed.

source.quote: Commence Royal Commission of Inquiry into Social Care System A national plan is critical for a sustainable social care system. The sector needs flexibility, tax incentives, VAT breaks and less waste. Simplify social care through a single funding stream, instead of the split between NHS and Local Authorities. More funding will be needed when a national plan is agreed.

bearing_set.reason: Social care access, cost, and sustainability are core O8 indicators; this policy commits to a structured reform process with funding contingent on a national plan, directly affecting security and dignity in later life.

Social care system reform bears on NHS capacity through the hospital-discharge/bed-blocking interface (an explicit O3 indicator); a more sustainable care sector reduces delayed transfers of care and improves healthcare access.

membership_note: The Commission is a process mechanism, but it is uniquely targeted at social care and makes conditional funding and structural-reform commitments, so it earns a genuine (if procedurally mediated) verdict on O8. The mention of tax incentives and VAT breaks is aspirational/within scope rather than a committed fiscal change, so O11 and O12 do not clear the non-negligible bar. No other fundamental has a concrete mechanism to evaluate.
